title: Matched Examples from a Split Sample
statement: Let $n,R,M$ be nonnegative integers, let $P$ be a subset of the $n$ coordinates, and let $z$ assign a sign in $\\{ -1,1 \\}$ to each coordinate in $P$. Let a Boolean function assign a sign to every sign vector, and let each of $R$ samples be formed by combining a fixed assignment on $P$ with a free assignment off $P$, then labeling the combined vector by the function. If at least $M$ of the fixed assignments equal $z$, then selecting the first $M$ such samples and retaining their free assignments and labels gives exactly the batch obtained by applying the function to those free assignments with $z$ fixed on $P$; in particular, the option-valued selection is defined and equals this batch.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a subset of the $n$ coordinates
A Boolean function maps sign vectors to signs
